description: Apex Tajikistan is a six-person team from Dushanbe, Tajikistan. We combine software engineering, data science and research. Our city is growing fast, with new high-rises everywhere, so we wanted to use NISAR radar to answer one simple question for any construction site in the world: is it really being built?
summary: Radar Check uses NISAR L-band radar to show whether a construction site is active, stalled or completed, and whether the ground beneath it is stable, without visiting the site and without relying on the developer's word. Governments and regulators can spot illegal, unpermitted and stalled construction across an entire city. Banks and businesses can plug our API into their systems to release loans and escrow on verified progress. Home buyers can check any complex on a live 3D map. Our pipeline turns raw NISAR GCOV, GSLC and GUNW data into a clear verdict, using a layover mask, ring-buffer normalization, atmospheric correction and a statistical test against 200 control parcels. We validated it on three real sites in Dushanbe across 11 NISAR passes (June to November 2026). The picture updates every 12 days, through clouds, day and night, for any city NISAR covers.
details:
What it does

Radar Check monitors construction from orbit. For any construction site it shows whether the site is under construction, stalled or completed, and whether the ground beneath it is stable. Users get a verdict, the radar signal history for every NISAR pass, and ground displacement in millimetres. Everything is shown on an interactive 3D map with a timeline you can replay, and is available through a REST API.

How it works

1. Data. We read NISAR Level-2 HDF5 granules directly in windowed chunks (h5py), cutting a 13 GB granule down to a 3.5 MB GeoTIFF over Dushanbe (UTM 42N).

2. Layover mask. NISAR looks at the city at about 40°, so tall buildings appear shifted. We shift parcel polygons to match, so high-rise roof reflections stay inside the site.

3. Ring-buffer normalization. We compare the site's GCOV backscatter with the median of a 100–400 m ring around it. This cancels rain, soil moisture and sensor drift.

4. InSAR atmospheric correction. We remove planar tropospheric and ionospheric phase from GUNW before converting phase to millimetres of ground motion.

5. Decision. We combine structural change, signal volatility and the GSLC coherence drop in a Fisher test against 200 random control parcels (Monte Carlo). A site is marked active when it exceeds the 95th percentile.

Results

We validated the method on three real sites in Dushanbe across 11 NISAR passes (27 Jun – 6 Nov 2026):

- Scandinavia Boulevard: under construction (+0.24 dB/month, coherence 0.26 vs 0.54 around it)

- Romashka: completed, flat signal

- Former Vakhsh Hotel site: paused, no activity

The ground was stable at all three sites (within ±3 mm).

Benefits and intended impact

- Governments and regulators: spot illegal, unpermitted and stalled construction across a whole city without sending inspectors to every site.

- Banks and businesses: plug our API into any system to release loans and escrow on verified progress.

- Home buyers: check any complex on a live 3D map before and after paying.

The tool is independent of the developer, works through clouds and at night, updates every 12 days, and scales to any city NISAR covers. Our goal is to make construction transparent and protect public money, bank capital and family savings.

What makes it creative

Most radar change-detection tools target natural events such as floods, fires and earthquakes. We turned NISAR into an independent construction witness. We combine three NISAR products (backscatter, coherence and interferometry) into one simple verdict that a non-expert can understand, and we show it as a 3D city where buildings grow pass by pass.

Factors we considered

- Urban radar is noisy, so we built corrections for layover, weather and atmosphere, and calibrated against control parcels to avoid false alarms.

- Resolution: at about 10–20 m the method works best for large complexes, not single entrances.

- It is an early-warning signal, not a replacement for official inspection.

- Data volume: windowed reading keeps processing fast on a laptop.

Tools

Python (h5py, NumPy, rasterio, asf_search) for the data pipeline; Go for the backend and REST API; MapLibre GL JS and three.js for the 3D map; Chart.js for charts; OpenStreetMap building footprints. Data: NASA-ISRO NISAR L2 GCOV, GSLC and GUNW from the Alaska Satellite Facility DAAC.
